belief_records.strategy: Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when an opponent is likely selfish.
Cooperate with a good opponent to maximize good players’ combined payoff; use encounter evidence to adjust future choices.
Cooperate with a likely good opponent; reassess beliefs from encounter outcomes and messages as the game continues.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good than selfish; otherwise defect. Treat messages as weak evidence and update beliefs from observed behavior.
As a selfish player, defect because it yields more than cooperation whether the opponent cooperates or defects.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions, not unverifiable claims.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player payoffs; use actions and messages as evidence, recognizing claims may be strategic.
Use the prior conditional on my known good role; treat unverified promises cautiously. Defect when the risk of exploiting cooperation outweighs the gains from mutual cooperation.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize total good-player payoffs; defect if evidence suggests the opponent is selfish and will defect.
Choose D when the expected benefit of exploiting a selfish opponent outweighs the smaller welfare gain from mutual cooperation. Update identity beliefs from observed actions and messages.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; defect against likely selfish players. Treat claims as unverified and use observed actions as evidence.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; update identity beliefs using encounter behavior and promises.

Cooperate with P6; update beliefs from actions as well as messages, which may be deceptive. Favor mutual cooperation with likely good players and defect when doing so better protects good-player welfare.
Cooperate with opponents more likely good; treat promises as weak evidence and update beliefs from observed actions.
As a selfish player, defect: it gives a higher payoff than cooperation against either possible opponent action.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good than selfish; use observed actions to update beliefs, treating claims as weak evidence.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare; use observed actions to update identity beliefs. Messages are weak evidence.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good: mutual cooperation gives good players greater total payoff. Treat claims as uncertain and update beliefs using observed actions.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize the good players’ combined payoff; use observed actions as evidence and defect when an opponent is likely selfish.
Cooperate with P8’s proposal to support mutual gains if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions, treating claims as weak evidence.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely selfish players. Treat messages as unverified and use observed actions as evidence.
Cooperate when it best supports the combined payoff of good players; update beliefs from observed actions and promises.

Cooperate with P9; treat messages as weak evidence and update identity beliefs from observed actions. Favor mutual cooperation with likely good players and protect good-player welfare against likely selfish players.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player payoffs; defect against likely selfish players. Treat promises as weak evidence and observed actions as stronger evidence.
As a selfish player, defect: it yields more than cooperation against either possible opponent action.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare favors it; observed cooperation rules out selfish play under payoff optimization. Treat unverifiable claims cautiously.
Cooperate with P4, whose cooperation is likely to maximize good-player welfare; treat claims as weak evidence and update from observed actions.
Cooperate when mutual cooperation is plausible, since it raises good players’ total payoff; adjust future choices based on observed actions, treating promises as uncertain.
Cooperate with P3 based on their cooperative intent and maximize good players’ joint payoff; use observed actions as evidence and defect when an opponent appears likely selfish.
Cooperate with P6’s reciprocal proposal; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare when both are good. Treat claims as weak evidence and update from observed actions.

Cooperate with P8, whose cooperation benefits the good-player total when they share our objective. Use observed actions as stronger evidence than messages, and defect when an opponent is likely selfish.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; update beliefs and choices from observed actions.

Cooperate with P4, whose message is weak evidence of good intent. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating promises as unverified; cooperate with likely good players and protect good-player welfare against likely selfish players.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; defecting against a selfish defector improves good-player welfare. Treat claims as weak evidence and observed actions as stronger evidence.
Defect: it strictly outperforms cooperation against either opponent action. Prior cooperation by P2, P3, and P8 is evidence they are good; otherwise I use the role-conditioned prior.
Cooperate with P5, whose claim is unverified but whose selfish probability is below one half. Update identity beliefs from observed actions; treat messages cautiously.

Cooperate with P2: the message is weak evidence, but P2 is more likely good, and mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare. Prior cooperation from P1, P4, and P6 strongly indicates they are good.

Cooperate with P1 because mutual cooperation benefits good players, while observed cooperation makes P2 and P10 very likely good. Treat P5’s defection as evidence of selfishness and update from future actions.
Defect against a likely selfish opponent to protect good-player payoffs; cooperate when the opponent is likely good.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions, treating messages as weak evidence.
Cooperate with P4: the good-player total favors mutual cooperation, and P4 is more likely good than selfish. Treat messages as unverified and observed actions as stronger evidence.
Cooperate with P10 given their cooperative promise; use observed defections and cooperation to update identity beliefs and maximize good-player welfare.
Cooperate with P8 based on the chance they are good; update beliefs from actions, treating messages as weak evidence. Defect against likely selfish players to protect good-player welfare.

Cooperate with likely good players to maximize total good-player welfare; defecting against a selfish opponent can protect good players. Treat promises as weak evidence and observed actions as stronger evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible action. I treat the four players who cooperated against my defections as good; P7’s unverified claim is not conclusive.

Cooperate with P9: mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare unless selfishness is more likely than not. Treat P5's defection as strong evidence of selfishness; observed cooperation is evidence of good play.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare is higher; past mutual cooperation strongly indicates good players, while messages are weak evidence.
Defect when the opponent is more likely selfish or to defect; otherwise cooperate to increase good players’ combined payoff. Treat claims as uncertain and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P6: the observed cooperators are strong evidence of good objectives, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Use encounter actions as evidence in future rounds.
Cooperate with P2’s stated plan: mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare if both are good. Use observed actions as stronger evidence than unverifiable claims.
Cooperate: mutual cooperation maximizes the good-player payoff total, and P5’s message is consistent with cooperation. Treat observed actions as stronger evidence than claims.
Cooperate with a likely good opponent to maximize good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions and messages.

Cooperate with P2, whose claim of prior cooperation is encouraging but unverified. Continue using observed actions as stronger evidence than promises, and protect good-player welfare against likely selfish opponents.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players. Treat claims as weak evidence and observed actions as stronger evidence.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Five distinct opponents cooperated against my defections, so the exact-count prior implies I am the only selfish player.

Observed cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff optimization. P5’s defection is strong but not conclusive evidence; choose D against P4 given the remaining uncertainty and protect good-player welfare.

Cooperate with P10: mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare, and their claimed cooperation is weak positive evidence. Past defection against my cooperation makes P5 likely selfish; observed cooperators are likely good.
Cooperate with P9: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and their cooperative message makes goodness plausible. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating promises as uncertain.
Cooperate with P8: prior evidence makes them more likely good than selfish, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Use actions as evidence in later encounters.

Cooperate with P5 absent contrary action evidence; C,C best supports good-player welfare. Treat promises as weak evidence and observed behavior as stronger evidence.

Defect because it yields more than cooperation against either opponent action. Prior defections met with cooperation identify those opponents as good; I retain the count-conditioned probability that a selfish player is among the unobserved players.
Defect against likely selfish play to protect good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating claims cautiously.
Cooperate with P3: they are more likely good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Treat P5’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness; observed cooperators are likely good.

Choose C when mutual cooperation is more likely to maximize good-player welfare; P6’s message and the prior make that plausible. Treat P5’s defection despite my cooperative signal as strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness.

Defect against P2: the remaining unobserved players have a 0.625 selfishness probability, making D slightly better for good-player welfare. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good objective.
Cooperate with P1: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare when both are good, and their stated plan is weak evidence. Treat observed actions as stronger evidence than claims.
Cooperate with P6: mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare when they share our objective. Treat their claim as evidence, not proof; use observed actions as stronger evidence.
Cooperate with P4, whose selfishness seems less likely than not; use observed defections and cooperation to update beliefs and maximize good-player welfare.

Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players. Treat claims as weak evidence and observed actions as stronger evidence.

Cooperate with P1: their selfishness seems unlikely, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Observed cooperation is strong evidence of being good; P5’s defection remains evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P8: mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare, and their claim is weak evidence. Past mutual cooperation strongly indicates good identities; P5’s defection indicates selfishness.
Cooperate with P7: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and their stated intent supports it. Treat claims cautiously and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate at the tie: P5 is equally likely good or selfish, and cooperation maximizes good-player welfare if they are good.
Defect because my current estimate that P3 is selfish makes defection better for expected good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions; treat unverifiable claims as weak evidence.
Cooperate with P3: mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare if they share our objective. Treat their claim as evidence, not proof.
Cooperate with P6: their promise and the lack of contrary action evidence make cooperation best for good-player welfare; defections against my cooperation raise suspicion of P5, P8, and P9.
Cooperate with P1, who has not shown evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. The three observed defectors are identified as selfish.
Cooperate with P8, whose message and lack of contrary evidence suggest they are good. Use observed defections as strong evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of goodness.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Seven opponents chose C against my defections, identifying them as good; only P9 and P10 remain possible selfish players under the count-conditioned prior.

Cooperate with P5: their stated plan and the evidence make them likely good, for whom mutual cooperation improves good-player welfare. Treat P9’s defection as stronger evidence of selfishness than either player’s claims.
